messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Borealis QBR prep — initial health snapshot + renewal watch (action items)

Team,

Attached is v2 of the Borealis QBR packet: a one-page health snapshot (PDF) and the renewal risk register (spreadsheet). High level context: Borealis is at a mid-stage renewal (contract expires 2027-05-15) and usage has dipped ~12% after they moved a batch workload to another provider. Procurement has already opened a pricing conversation (see external thread I’ve cc'd below).

What I need from this group by EOD Feb 12:
- Everyone: review the risk register and update the OWNER column for any rows you take (column G).
- Sales (Aditya): propose a constrained concession plan (max discount, term swap options) and add to the "Commercial Options" tab.
- Legal/Security (Laura): confirm whether the SSO and data retention asks change our position — mark any items that require legal review.
- Ops/Customer Success (Grace): confirm whether the recent performance incidents are mitigated and add the operational remediation ETA.
- Leadership (Rishi): I’m looking for a short exec ask (1–2 bullets) we can share in tomorrow’s leadership huddle if we need sign-off quickly.

Top 3 candidate exec flags I see today (please validate/adjust):
1) Renewal economics: procurement asking for a 20% price concession tied to a 12-month renewal — high impact to ACV.
2) Performance degradations in late-January batch runs (impact: nightly ingest) — customer wants a technical deep-dive and SLA credits.
3) SSO + data-retention contract language — legal review needed for a special clause.

Attachments: borealis_qbr_risk_register_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), borealis_health_snapshot_Feb2027.pdf (one-pager).

Please use the "ExecAsk" sheet in the spreadsheet for any ask you think needs an exec sign-off — keep asks short, include the trade (what we give vs what we ask). If you think an offer is reasonable, add the suggested concession and the minimum acceptable term (ex: 10% off for a 12‑month extension).

CCing the Borealis procurement thread below for context (María). I will consolidate and prepare the one-page exec brief for distribution by Feb 13 10:00am PT.

Thanks,

Diego Fernandez
Sr. Account Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Borealis QBR prep — initial health snapshot + renewal watch (action items)

Thanks Diego — I’ll take the legal/security items. Quick notes after a skim of the register:
- SSO: Borealis is requesting SCIM + enforced SSO for all service accounts. Legal flagged potential implementation SLA language and an indemnity clause. I’ll mark those rows as "Legal Review" and add a recommended clause in column H.
- Data retention: they want a 7-year audit log retention option in writing; we have a compliance package but this will require a new addendum — estimating 5 business days for review.

I’ll update the register by tomorrow morning and flag anything that requires exec sign-off.

Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Borealis QBR prep — commercial options + suggested concession cap

Diego — taking the commercial options. Notes added to the spreadsheet (Commercial Options tab). TL;DR: I recommend we hold to a max concession of 12% on list price for a 12‑month renewal with the following trade:
- 12% off ARR for 12 months in exchange for a firm 12-month renewal (no early termination).
- Offer a technical deep-dive within 7 business days and a one-time remediation credit capped at $30k (to compensate for the January incident).
- If they push for SCIM/SSO SLA language, offer a 6-month implementation SLA commitment and a tech resources guarantee — do not bake indemnities into the commercial offer.

If leadership wants to be more aggressive we can expand to a 15% cap + quarterly usage commitments, but prefer to keep the first offer conservative.

Attachment: Borealis_MutualActionPlan.docx (draft MPA).

Subject: Re: Borealis QBR prep — exec attention: ask for guidance

Team — good work pulling this together. I reviewed the risk register this morning. My recommended exec asks (short bullets for the leadership huddle):
1) Approve a one-time remediation credit up to $50k to settle the January performance incident contingent on a signed 12-month renewal at the 12% concession level Aditya proposed.
2) Authorize a SOC/SSO implementation commitment (6 month SLA) to be included as an appendix — legal to confirm final language.

Rationale: the credit reduces near-term churn risk and the SLA commitment addresses the customer's trust gap. Cost/benefit: $50k credit vs ~60% probability of a 12-month renewal at current health (modeled in the spreadsheet).

I need a leadership green light by today 4:00pm PT to include the offer in the outbound commercial response to Borealis procurement. If we do not get a decision by 4pm, I recommend we proceed with Aditya’s conservative 12% + $30k credit plan.
